[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Serverfarm describes itself as a global data center developer and operator with more than 25 years of operating experience, focused on AI-ready, build-to-suit, high-density facilities. The operators homepage did not state a headquarters address, exact founding year, or ownership structure.

The companys site lists nine operational North American locations, Clarksville, Atlanta, Chicago, two in Houston, Los Angeles, Northern Virginia, Moses Lake, Washington, and Toronto, Canada, plus three in Europe and the Middle East, Amsterdam, London, and two in Israel, with additional sites described as coming soon. Trade press and Serverfarms own press release describe the company acquiring a 12 megawatt Los Angeles data center in El Segundo from T5 Data Centers, another operator separately tracked in this registry, for approximately $71 million, a direct example of a facility changing hands between two operators already profiled here.

The registry here tracks 2 Serverfarm facilities across two states, California and Illinois. The California facility is a strong candidate to be the same El Segundo, Los Angeles building acquired from T5, a specific lead this registrys facility-level research phase should verify directly rather than treat as a fresh Serverfarm build, recording a former_operator relationship to T5 if confirmed. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading.body:
Serverfarm CH1 sits at 840 South Canal Street in Chicago's Near West Side, in Cook County. The facility's published power capacity is not stated in the data provided. Without a megawatt figure, the campus cannot be ranked against other Illinois facilities by IT load, though state context shows it ranks seventh among the six Illinois facilities with published capacity, indicating either a data inconsistency or that this facility's capacity falls below the threshold of the sixth-largest published site.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities across the state, of which only six publish power figures totaling 236 megawatts. Serverfarm operates two facilities tracked in this registry, one in Illinois and one in California. The operator describes itself as focused on AI-ready, high-density builds with more than 25 years of operating experience and nine operational North American locations, but the specific certifications, power draw, and tenant suitability of CH1 are not published.

The data necessary to assess whether this campus matters to AI scaling—its IT load in megawatts, power delivery infrastructure, cooling capacity, and grid interconnection—has not been published by the operator. Without these specifications, CH1 cannot be evaluated against the constraint binding AI deployment, which this site holds to be available power and grid headroom.
